title: At the Pharmacy
subtitle: でかけるまえに・カウンターで・くすりののみかた・ただいま
register: casual at home, polite (desu/masu) at the counter
review: Kana, kanji (say), translations, notes and questions written by Claude from Marissa's romaji script. The Japanese has not been checked by a Japanese speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines yet. The pharmacist is read by Jap-yuyu (r4qMc0xxpfgMQciUmPHW), a man's voice, as the course has no second woman's voice; the English lines say 'they' for the pharmacist.
intro: Riku has a cold and is sure it is the end, so Emi goes to the pharmacy for him: four short scenes. Listen for how she asks for medicine with … ga hoshii n desu ga, for the pharmacist's polite questions, and for how to say how often and how long to take something.

lines.romaji: Emi… boku wa mō dame da.
lines.kana: エミ…ぼくはもうだめだ。
lines.say: エミ…僕はもうだめだ。
lines.note: Mō dame da: it's all over. Boku: I, used by men and boys.

lines.kana: ただのかぜでしょ。
lines.say: ただの風邪でしょ。
lines.note: Tada no: just an ordinary… Kaze: a cold. Desho: surely, right?

lines.romaji: Nodo ga itai. Atama mo itai. Zenbu itai.
lines.kana: のどがいたい。あたまもいたい。ぜんぶいたい。
lines.say: 喉が痛い。頭も痛い。全部痛い。

tr.en: My throat hurts. My head hurts too. Everything hurts.

lines.note: Part of the body + ga itai: it hurts. Mo: too. Zenbu: all of it.

lines.romaji: Yakkyoku ni itte kuru ne. Nani ga iru?
lines.kana: やっきょくにいってくるね。なにがいる？
lines.say: 薬局に行ってくるね。何がいる？

tr.en: I'll go to the pharmacy. What do you need?

lines.note: Yakkyoku: a pharmacy. Itte kuru: to go and come back. Iru: to need; what you need takes ga.

lines.kana: きせき。
lines.say: 奇跡。
lines.note: Kiseki: a miracle.

lines.romaji: Shohōsen nashi de kaeru ka, kiite miru.
lines.kana: しょほうせんなしでかえるか、きいてみる。
lines.say: 処方箋なしで買えるか、聞いてみる。

tr.en: I'll ask if you can get one without a prescription.

lines.note: Shohōsen: a prescription. Nashi de: without. Kaeru: can buy. Kiite miru: to try asking.

lines.romaji: Sumimasen, kazegusuri ga hoshii n desu ga.
lines.kana: すみません、かぜぐすりがほしいんですが。
lines.say: すみません、風邪薬が欲しいんですが。

tr.en: Excuse me, I'd like some cold medicine.

lines.note: Kazegusuri: cold medicine (kaze + kusuri). … ga hoshii n desu ga: I'd like…; the ga at the end leaves the request soft and open.

lines.kana: はい。どなたがのまれますか？
lines.say: はい。どなたが飲まれますか？

tr.en: Of course. Who will be taking it?

lines.note: Donata: who, polite. Nomaremasu: the respectful form of nomu. In Japanese, medicine is drunk: kusuri o nomu.

lines.kana: おっとです。
lines.say: 夫です。
lines.note: Otto: my husband. Someone else's husband: goshujin.

lines.kana: どんなしょうじょうですか？
lines.say: どんな症状ですか？
lines.note: Shōjō: symptoms. Donna: what kind of.

lines.romaji: Hanamizu to seki ga dete, monku mo ōi desu.
lines.kana: はなみずとせきがでて、もんくもおおいです。
lines.say: 鼻水と咳が出て、文句も多いです。

tr.en: He has a runny nose and a cough, and a lot of complaints.

lines.note: Hanamizu: a runny nose. Seki: a cough. … ga deru: it comes out. Monku: complaints. Ōi: many.

lines.kana: ねつはありますか？
lines.say: 熱はありますか？
lines.note: Netsu: a fever. … wa arimasu ka: is there…?, do you have…?

lines.romaji: Sanjūnana-do ni-bu desu. Honnin wa jūshō da to itte imasu.
lines.kana: さんじゅうななどにぶです。ほんにんはじゅうしょうだといっています。
lines.say: さんじゅうななどにぶです。本人は重症だと言っています。

tr.en: Thirty-seven point two. He says it's serious.

lines.note: 37.2 is sanjūnana-do ni-bu: degrees (do) and tenths (bu). Honnin: the person himself. Jūshō: a serious case. … to itte imasu: he says that…

lines.kana: アレルギーはありますか？
lines.note: Arerugī: an allergy, from the German Allergie.

lines.kana: かじだけです。
lines.say: 家事だけです。
lines.note: Kaji: housework. Dake: only. He is not really allergic: he doesn't like doing it.

lines.romaji: Kono sekidome wa, asa to yoru ni nonde kudasai.
lines.kana: このせきどめは、あさとよるにのんでください。
lines.say: この咳止めは、朝と夜に飲んでください。

tr.en: Take this cough medicine in the morning and at night.

lines.note: Sekidome: cough medicine (seki + tomeru, to stop). Nonde kudasai: please take it.

lines.kana: わかりました。じょうざいは？
lines.say: わかりました。錠剤は？
lines.note: Jōzai: tablets. … wa? with a rising voice: and…?

lines.romaji: Ichi-nichi san-kai, shokugo ni ichi-jō desu.
lines.kana: いちにちさんかい、しょくごにいちじょうです。
lines.say: いちにちさんかい、食後にいちじょうです。

tr.en: One tablet three times a day, after meals.

lines.note: Ichi-nichi san-kai: three times a day. Shokugo: after meals; shokuzen: before meals. Jō counts tablets.

lines.kana: なんにちくらいのみますか？
lines.say: なんにちくらい飲みますか？
lines.note: Nan-nichi: how many days. Kurai: about.

lines.romaji: Itsuka-kan made desu. Yoku naranakereba, byōin ni itte kudasai.
lines.kana: いつかかんまでです。よくならなければ、びょういんにいってください。
lines.say: いつかかんまでです。良くならなければ、病院に行ってください。

tr.en: Up to five days. If he doesn't get better, he should go to the doctor.

lines.note: Itsuka-kan: five days. Made: up to. Yoku naranakereba: if he doesn't get better. Byōin: a hospital or a doctor's office.

lines.kana: しょほうせんはいりますか？
lines.say: 処方箋はいりますか？
lines.note: Irimasu: is needed. Irimasen: is not needed.

lines.romaji: Iie, irimasen. Sen nihyaku en desu.
lines.kana: いいえ、いりません。せんにひゃくえんです。
lines.note: Sen nihyaku en: 1,200 yen.

lines.kana: カードでおねがいします。
lines.say: カードでお願いします。
lines.note: … de onegai shimasu: with…, please. In cash: genkin de.

lines.kana: どうだった？なんていってた？
lines.say: どうだった？何て言ってた？

tr.en: How did it go? What did they say?

lines.note: Dō datta?: how was it? Nan te itteta?: the casual form of nan to itte imashita ka.

lines.romaji: Jōzai wa ichi-nichi san-kai, sekidome wa asa to yoru.
lines.kana: じょうざいはいちにちさんかい、せきどめはあさとよる。
lines.say: 錠剤はいちにちさんかい、咳止めは朝と夜。

tr.en: The tablets three times a day, the cough medicine morning and night.

lines.note: Wa marks each topic: as for the tablets…, as for the cough medicine…

lines.kana: いつまでねていればいい？
lines.say: いつまで寝ていればいい？

tr.en: How long should I stay in bed?

lines.note: Itsu made: until when. Nete iru: to be lying down. … ba ii?: should I…?

lines.romaji: Konban kara sara-arai shite ii tte.
lines.kana: こんばんからさらあらいしていいって。
lines.say: 今晩から皿洗いしていいって。

tr.en: They said you can do the dishes from tonight.

lines.note: Konban kara: from tonight. Sara-arai: washing the dishes. Shite ii: you may do it. Tte: they said, a casual quotation.

lines.kana: ほんとうにそういったの？
lines.say: 本当にそう言ったの？
lines.note: Hontō ni: really. Sō itta: said so.

lines.kana: はこにかいてあるよ。
lines.say: 箱に書いてあるよ。
lines.note: Hako: a box. Kaite aru: it is written. She is joking.

notes: Asking at the pharmacy: kazegusuri ga hoshii n desu ga (I'd like some cold medicine).
Symptoms: nodo ga itai, atama ga itai; hanamizu ga deru, seki ga deru; netsu ga aru.
The pharmacist's polite questions: Donata ga nomaremasu ka? Donna shōjō desu ka? Netsu wa arimasu ka? Arerugī wa arimasu ka?
Medicine is drunk: kusuri o nomu. Ichi-nichi san-kai, shokugo ni ichi-jō: one tablet three times a day, after meals. Asa to yoru: morning and night.
Shohōsen: a prescription. Irimasu ka? (is it needed?) Iie, irimasen (no, it isn't).
Numbers: 37.2 is sanjūnana-do ni-bu; 1,200 yen is sen nihyaku en. Paying: kādo de, genkin de.
Reporting words: … to itte imasu (he says that…), casual … tte (they said…).

questions.q: How does Emi ask for cold medicine?
options: Kazegusuri ga hoshii n desu ga.
Kaze ga hoshii n desu ga.
questions.why: Kazegusuri: cold medicine. … ga hoshii n desu ga: I'd like…

questions.q: What does Emi say about Riku's symptoms?
options: Hanamizu to seki ga dete, monku mo ōi.
questions.why: A runny nose and a cough, and a lot of complaints.

questions.q: How does Riku take the tablets?
questions.why: The cough medicine is asa to yoru; the tablets: ichi-nichi san-kai, shokugo ni ichi-jō.
Iie, irimasen: no, it isn't needed.

questions.q: Is Riku really allergic to housework?
options: Yes: kaji o suru to seki ga deru.
No. Emi means he doesn't like doing it.
questions.why: Kaji dake desu: Emi is joking.
